- Is Bookkeeping a Good Career in 2026?


Bookkeeping is still a realistic career path in 2026, with the[Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/office-and-administrative-support/bookkeeping-accounting-and-auditing-clerks.htm#tab-6) projecting roughly 144,100 job openings each year through 2035. Nearly all of those annual openings come from replacing workers who retire or move into other occupations rather than from new positions being created.


But before you pursue a career in bookkeeping, it helps to know exactly what bookkeepers do, the most common challenges of the role, and how to prepare for your next opportunity.


## **Key Points**


- Bookkeepers track and record financial transactions on behalf of businesses. Their work gives companies a clear picture of their financial health and the confidence to make smarter operating decisions.
- Bookkeeping is a good career for the right person. Detail-oriented problem-solvers who communicate well and are comfortable with numbers are set up to thrive.
- You don’t need a four-year degree to get hired. BLS lists typical entry-level education as some college with no degree, and many employers hire candidates with a high school diploma plus relevant coursework.
- The role is changing thanks in large part to automation and artificial intelligence (AI), but the job outlook for bookkeepers remains relatively promising. The BLS projects roughly 144,100 openings every year through 2035, nearly all of them created by workers retiring or leaving the field.


## **What a Bookkeeper Actually Does Day to Day**


Bookkeepers record and track a business’s financial transactions to keep the books accurate and complete. On any given day, that might mean:


- Managing financial records like invoices, bills, purchase orders, and receipts
- Recording day-to-day financial transactions
- Handling payroll processes
- Tracking accounts payable and receivable (AP/AR)
- Supporting compliance with accounting processes and tax regulations
- Using software or databases to reconcile accounts or generate basic financial reports


Done well, that work gives business owners a clear read on cash flow, spending, and profitability. Those are the numbers businesses need to make informed decisions.


### **Bookkeeping vs. Accounting**


[Bookkeepers and accountants](https://www.intuit.com/blog/life-at-intuit/intuit-experts-bookkeeping-vs-accounting/) work together, but they’re not the same. Accountants prepare financial statements, like income statements and balance sheets, based on the information the bookkeeper provides. They then analyze those statements to identify trends or predict potential business risks and opportunities. Some accountants may also implement internal controls or conduct financial audits.


### **Where Bookkeepers Work**


Like other accounting professionals, bookkeepers can work for small businesses or firms across nearly any industry. Most work in an office setting, but some offer their services remotely. Bookkeepers also tend to work full time, though businesses may require overtime during tax season and at the fiscal year’s end.


## **Is Bookkeeping in Demand Right Now?**


Yes, bookkeepers are in demand, but with one important caveat. The BLS projects a 6% decline in total employment for bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks between 2025 and 2035, while still projecting about 144,100 openings each year. Those openings come from turnover, not growth. The roles exist, but competition for them is unlikely to ease.


Technological advancements, particularly in automation software and AI, have changed the way bookkeeping is done. These technologies can handle routine tasks like data entry and basic report generation.


In a[2025 Intuit QuickBooks survey](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/r/news/intuit-quickbooks-tech-survey/) , 95% of accounting professionals said their firms had adopted automation technologies in the past year, including for payroll processing, accounts payable and receivable, and data entry and transaction processing.


Small and medium-sized businesses still need[skilled bookkeepers](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-finance-and-accounting-roles-are-in-highest-demand#toc3) to keep their records accurate and up to date. They also need bookkeepers to help protect their financial data and make sense of the numbers.


What’s changing is where bookkeepers spend their time (and energy). It’s less about manual, repetitive tasks and more about analytical or advisory work. That includes:


- Analyzing trends in the books
- Interpreting financial data for owners who aren’t well-versed in accounting
- Advising on cash flow, spending, and growth decisions
- Catching the errors and edge cases that automation misses


Matters requiring human judgment or face-to-face communication also aren’t going away, even with parts of the job being automated.


## **Skills and Training That Help You Get Started**


Bookkeeping is widely considered an entry-level role, meaning you don’t need years of experience to get hired. The BLS lists the typical entry-level education for bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks as some college with no degree. Many employers will also consider candidates with a high school diploma who have completed relevant coursework.


If you don’t have a background in the field, taking[bookkeeping courses](https://www.intuit.com/blog/life-at-intuit/bookkeeping-course/) can help you build a foundation. Whichever path you take, the role calls for a specific mix of hard and soft skills:


### **Hard Skills**


- Bookkeeping software proficiency, starting with QuickBooks and Excel
- Financial data analysis and interpretation (business’s financial statements)
- Records management
- Payroll management
- Working knowledge of tax rules and financial regulations


### **Soft Skills**


- Attention to detail for catching errors and inconsistencies
- Clear written and verbal communication with clients and stakeholders
- Problem-solving and judgment
- Time management, especially during tax season
- Adaptability as the role continues to shift


Besides courses, you can pick up these skills through practical training or certifications. Two of the more recognized bookkeeping programs:


- [Certified Bookkeeper](https://aipb.org/certification-program/) (American Institute of Professional Bookkeepers)
- [Certified Public Bookkeeper](https://www.nacpb.org/) (National Association of Certified Public Bookkeepers)


Another option is a[bookkeeping badge through Intuit Academy](https://academy.intuit.com/user-focus/qualify-for-role-intuit) . Badges are not a guarantee of employment, but they may help you qualify for some roles at Intuit.


## **The Upsides and Challenges of Bookkeeping Work**


Bookkeeping is still a good career in 2026. That said, every career has trade-offs, and bookkeeping is no exception.


According to[Robert Half](https://www.roberthalf.com/us/en/insights/research/data-reveals-which-finance-and-accounting-roles-are-in-highest-demand#toc3) , bookkeeping has above-average growth and consistent demand, with starting salaries in the range of $55,000. Other benefits of becoming a bookkeeper include:


- **Exposure to multiple industries:** Bookkeepers work across basically every sector, from healthcare to tech. It’s a role that transfers well.
- **Work-life balance:** Bookkeepers usually work a standard weekday schedule. This predictable schedule can be a major plus.
- **Remote opportunities:** While many bookkeepers work in the office, some work remotely.
- **Low barrier of entry:** Bookkeepers don’t generally need a college education or certification to get hired. This makes it more accessible for those just getting started or making a career shift.


Bookkeeping isn’t without its challenges, though. Here’s what to know going in:


- **Deadline pressure:** Businesses need reliable bookkeepers who can meet filing deadlines and close books on time.
- **Fluctuating workloads:** While much of the year is consistent, busy seasons like tax time or the end of the fiscal year often call for longer hours.
- **Need for sustained accuracy:** Bookkeepers are responsible for keeping accurate, complete financial records and ensuring regulatory compliance, even during heavy workloads.
- **Repetitive work:** Automation software has taken some of the load off, but bookkeepers still often need to handle some routine tasks. That includes data entry or invoice processing, which can be repetitive.


Still interested?[Join our bookkeeping community](https://www.intuit.com/expert-careers/join-tax-bookkeeping-community/) today, and you’ll be the first to know about upcoming job opportunities and industry events.


## **How to Start Your Bookkeeping Career**


Here’s how to[become a bookkeeper](https://www.intuit.com/blog/life-at-intuit/intuit-experts/how-to-become-a-bookkeeper-a-complete-guide/) in 6 simple steps:


1. **Start learning core bookkeeping skills.** You’ll need soft skills (like communication and problem-solving) and technical skills (like account reconciliation and payroll basics). Get comfortable with common accounting software like Excel and QuickBooks, too.
2. **Enroll in a bookkeeping course.** YouTube tutorials, free courses, and Intuit’s own bookkeeping course are all reasonable starting points.
3. **Get certified.** While not required, a bookkeeping certification can help you stand out. Consider one from an accredited organization, like the NACPB or the AIPB. If you’re looking for a free option,[Intuit Academy](https://academy.intuit.com/courses/intuit-bookkeeping-certification) offers a Bookkeeping Professional badge that takes about 30 hours to complete.
4. **Start gaining experience.** Even volunteering to handle a local nonprofit’s books can help build your skills. Working as a freelance bookkeeper or interning at a small accounting firm can also give you practical experience.
5. **Put together your resume.** Your[bookkeeper resume](https://www.intuit.com/blog/life-at-intuit/intuit-experts-bookkeeper-resume/) should include your core skills and experience accumulated through professional-level or volunteer work. It should also list related software proficiency and educational background.
6. **Apply.** Start applying for entry-level bookkeeping roles. It helps to include a cover letter with each application.


## **Start Your Bookkeeping Career With Intuit**


The bookkeeping career outlook is positive for people who lean into where the work is going. Even with AI and automation disrupting the field, employers need analytical minds and human judgment to support decision-making. That goes as much for bookkeepers as it does other finance or accounting pros.


If you’re looking for a flexible opportunity with steady demand and a relatively low barrier to entry, explore[bookkeeping jobs](https://www.intuit.com/expert-careers/bookkeeping-jobs/?cid=seo_blogs_tax_us_fy27_lg_bookkeeping_good_career_link_inti-tm) at Intuit. Many opportunities are remote.

## **FAQs**


###


Bookkeepers usually handle more repetitive, routine tasks than other tax or accounting professionals. Day-to-day tasks include data entry, invoice processing, and account reconciliation. Typically, bookkeepers also work a predictable schedule, though overtime may be required during busier seasons.


###


[Nearly half (47.24%)](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/careers/bookkeeping-accounting-and-auditing-clerk/education) of bookkeepers only have a high school diploma or less. That means that getting even a certificate can help you stand out from the competition. Consider a certification from the AIPB or the NACPB. For a starting-from-zero path, the free Intuit Academy Bookkeeping badge takes about 30 hours and qualifies you to apply for a QuickBooks role.


###


Once you’re working, a few paths open up. Earning the AIPB or NACPB certification signals competence and can help lead to higher-paying roles. College coursework in accounting or finance (or eventually a bachelor’s degree) opens the door to accounting-track positions. You can also specialize by industry (e.g., healthcare, nonprofits, real estate) or by service line, moving from transactional work into advisory or fractional chief financial officer (CFO)-style engagements with small business clients.
